messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache paging spike detected on cluster tp-shard-7. NCCL stall pattern observed + disk paging up from 0 -> 70% over 3m. Auto-suppress: false.
maya: oncall here, looking. where's the grafana link?
joel: grabbing logs from runtime. initial guess: continuous batching mem growth + uneven KV shard partitioning under TP.
siva: saw a similar signature yesterday when we pushed the 'dynamic-kv-shard' change — could be an edge-case for odd-numbered tensor-parallel groups.
maya: ops-bot, can you post the affected host list and pids?
ops-bot: hosts: tp-shard-7-{02,03,04}, worker pids: 2189, 2191, 2193. paging processes: runtime-server (pid 2189). link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-cache/kv-paging?orgId=1&from=now-15m
joel: pasting tail of runtime log (snipped):
```
E 19:04:11 runtime: kv_cache_shard: assigned_shard_counts=[1024,1024,512]
W 19:04:12 runtime: continuous_batcher queue_length=792, max_tokens_per_batch=4096
E 19:04:13 nccl: stall detected, sync timeout 120s, peer retry
E 19:04:13 memory: OOM soft -> swapping started
```
maya: that shard_counts array looks wrong — uneven partitioning (512 on one node). should be balanced.
ken: quick question — are we serving any high-prefix customers that could trigger runaway prefix caching?
elaine: CS update: two customers (acme-corp, beta-startup) reported elevated latency and timeouts on embeddings and chat endpoints. high severity for acme-corp.
siva: confirmed: dynamic-kv-shard algorithm miscomputes when TP group size is 3 and model sequence length > 8k. fallback path wasn't exercised because continuous batching increased prefix reuse. chain reaction -> huge per-host KV memory, eviction thrash -> paging.
maya: mitigation plan (short term): 1) disable dynamic-kv-shard on tp-shard-7, 2) reduce continuous_batcher max_tokens to 512, 3) route acme-corp traffic to dedicated fallback model (gpt-small-quant) until stable.
joel: agree. I'll push hotpatch to configmap and roll restart the runtime pods in that shard (one at a time).
deploy-bot: suggested command: `kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"dynamic_kv_shard":"false","continuous_batch_max_tokens":"512"}}'`
maya: do that with a canary first on tp-shard-7-04 (the one with 512 currently)
joel: doing canary now. patch applied to tp-shard-7-04, restarting pod runtime-server-04. logs tailing...
ops-bot: resource note: disk i/o still high on tp-shard-7-02 and 03. canary pod back up, reports balanced shard_counts=[850,850,850] and continuous_batcher queue reduced to 120.
joel: rolling restart on 02 -> patch -> 03.
maya: monitor latency and paging for each step. set alert threshold to 20% higher than baseline.
elaine: I sent a brief to acme-corp that we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA. they asked for ETA ~30-45m.
ken: small ops note: do we need to force eviction of oversized KV entries to speed recovery?
siva: yes, I pushed a soft-evict command to the canary: `curl -X POST http://runtime-server-04.internal/localadmin/kv/evict?threshold=0.75` — reduced memory footprint by ~22% in the canary.
maya: good. after 03 is done, run the evict across remaining nodes. also flag to disable dynamic-kv-shard in cluster config to prevent automated re-enable.
joel: 02 patched and restarted; 03 patch in progress.
deploy-bot: rolling restart completed on tp-shard-7 (03). all runtime pods report stable. paging dropped from 70% -> 6% in 12 minutes. NCCL stall alerts cleared.
maya: :white_check_mark: mitigation successful for now. customer impact: acme-corp latency returned to normal; beta-startup still reporting intermittent 500s — looks like they hit timeouts during thrash. Elaine can you coordinate a postmortem customer note?
elaine: on it. will provide timeline + mitigation steps.
ken: follow-up tasks: 1) revert dynamic-kv-shard experimental flag codepath to patch branch, 2) add unit tests for TP-group-size odd partitioning, 3) add guardrail in runtime to refuse imbalanced shard assignments, 4) add continuous_batcher backpressure thresholds.
siva: assigning myself to 1 & 2, joel take 3 & 4?
joel: taking 3 & 4. I'll open PRs and link here.
maya: handoff: I'm oncall for another 18m, then morning oncall (ken) will take over. summary for handoff: incident: KV cache paging due to dynamic-kv-shard + continuous batching. impact: degraded latency and NCCL stalls on tp-shard-7 affecting embeddings/chat for 2 customers. mitigation: disabled dynamic sharding, reduced batch max_tokens, soft-evict, rolled restarts. current state: stable, monitoring.
ken: I'll take over. please drop links to PRs + postmortem.
joel: opening PRs now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 (guardrail imbalance), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/483 (batcher backpressure).
siva: created hotfix revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/481 (revert dynamic-kv-shard experimental).
elaine: customer notes queued. will send ACME follow-up + scheduling for incident review.
maya: thanks everyone. leaving handoff.
inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. classified as Sev2. handoff to ken at 1936002500.
ken: acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and schedule the postmortem sync.
